builder_plan.scenario: A product assistant retrieves plausible documents but gives unsupported answers.
builder_plan.change: Change one retrieval or ranking step while keeping the document snapshot fixed.
builder_plan.baseline: Your current retrieval pipeline with identical questions and answer model.
steps: Locate the paper's implementation and check its license, model support, data needs, and hardware requirements. Stop here if you cannot obtain the required artifacts.
Save a small set of representative product tasks and expected outcomes. Keep evaluation tasks out of any training or tuning, and choose quality and cost limits before running.
Run the baseline and the proposed change on identical inputs. Keep other settings fixed and repeat paired runs to expose variation.
Save per-task outputs, failures, timings, and all usage costs. Review regressions before expanding the test.
builder_plan.measure: Supported answers, retrieval misses, correct abstentions, index cost, and response latency.
builder_plan.decision: Keep the change only if it meets your preselected quality and latency limits and improves the metric you care about after setup and operating costs. Otherwise retain the baseline. This is an exploration plan, not a validated recommendation.

title: KatoANN: Enabling Near-Exact Vector Search at the Speed of Lossy Scans with CPU Matrix Engines
summary: The method replaces memory-bound lossy distance scans (or a full-vector refinement pass) in partition-family ANN search with a batched rank-then-refine scan over a single 16-bit SQ16 code, using Intel AMX to reuse fetched codes across queries. Costs include 16-bit storage per vector plus the rank-refine scan logic, and it depends on Intel AMX CPU hardware and on batch query availability to shift the workload from memory-bound to compute-bound. It can fail under low query concurrency, where batching yields little reuse, on hardware without AMX, or on workloads where SQ16 high-byte ranking misidentifies survivors and recall degrades.
rationale: The technique is relevant to retrieval-heavy RAG pipelines but requires specific Intel AMX CPUs and batched query traffic that the reader's 24 GB GPU setup does not provide, so it warrants monitoring rather than adoption or testing now.
technique: Batched SQ16 ANN scan on Intel AMX

claims.statement: The method replaces memory-bound lossy distance scans (or a full-vector refinement pass) in partition-family ANN search with a batched rank-then-refine scan over a single 16-bit SQ16 code, using Intel AMX to reuse fetched codes across queries. Costs include 16-bit storage per vector plus the rank-refine scan logic, and it depends on Intel AMX CPU hardware and on batch query availability to shift the workload from memory-bound to compute-bound. It can fail under low query concurrency, where batching yields little reuse, on hardware without AMX, or on workloads where SQ16 high-byte ranking misidentifies survivors and recall degrades.

KatoANN is reported as the fastest partition-family ANN system in its evaluation across the high-recall range, achieving near-exact distances at lossy-scan speed by batching scans on Intel AMX; no single quantified speedup factor is stated in the abstract.
